rationale: The failure occurred because we landed on the locale homepage (/en-jp/) where no PLP tiles exist. Prioritizing settings-level fixes, we set a stable, directly-listing PLP kickoff URL (jackets) within the same locale and add an automatic redirect from the locale home to that PLP. URL normalization keeps us on moncler.com with the /en-jp prefix and avoids corporate/auxiliary domains like monclergroup.com. We avoid changing selectors since the core issue is entry-point/flow rather than DOM targeting; instead we provide code hints to accept cookies/geo modals and to fall back to robust PDP selectors.
code_hints: If current URL is a locale home like /en-jp/ and no PLP tiles appear within 6–8s, proactively navigate to /en-jp/men/ready-to-wear/jackets/?sz=120 (or the women fallback) and continue.
Handle cookie consent: if #onetrust-accept-btn-handler exists, click it immediately.
Handle potential geo/country modal: in any dialog, try clicking a primary button containing text: 'Continue', 'Japan', or 'Accept all'.

After landing on a PLP, wait for a product grid container such as: [data-testid="product-grid"], .product-grid, ul.products-grid, or [role='list'] with product cards, then scroll to the bottom once to trigger lazy load.
Extract PLP links by querying anchors within the grid first; keep locale segment (/en-jp) when resolving hrefs.

On PDP, try multiple price/title selectors; typical fallbacks: title -> h1[data-test='pdp-title'], h1.product-name, h1[itemprop='name']; price -> span[itemprop='price'], [data-test='pdp-price'], .price__value.
Ensure all navigations preserve https and the /en-jp locale; if a link drops the locale, rewrite it to include /en-jp before requesting.
